<div class="line"><a name="l01774"></a><span class="lineno"> 1774</span>&#160;<span class="comment">// Helper: Manually clip large list of items.</span></div>
<div class="line"><a name="l01775"></a><span class="lineno"> 1775</span>&#160;<span class="comment">// If you are submitting lots of evenly spaced items and you have a random access to the list, you can perform coarse clipping based on visibility to save yourself from processing those items at all.</span></div>
<div class="line"><a name="l01776"></a><span class="lineno"> 1776</span>&#160;<span class="comment">// The clipper calculates the range of visible items and advance the cursor to compensate for the non-visible items we have skipped.</span></div>
<div class="line"><a name="l01777"></a><span class="lineno"> 1777</span>&#160;<span class="comment">// ImGui already clip items based on their bounds but it needs to measure text size to do so. Coarse clipping before submission makes this cost and your own data fetching/submission cost null.</span></div>
<div class="line"><a name="l01778"></a><span class="lineno"> 1778</span>&#160;<span class="comment">// Usage:</span></div>
<div class="line"><a name="l01779"></a><span class="lineno"> 1779</span>&#160;<span class="comment">//     ImGuiListClipper clipper(1000);  // we have 1000 elements, evenly spaced.</span></div>
<div class="line"><a name="l01780"></a><span class="lineno"> 1780</span>&#160;<span class="comment">//     while (clipper.Step())</span></div>
<div class="line"><a name="l01781"></a><span class="lineno"> 1781</span>&#160;<span class="comment">//         for (int i = clipper.DisplayStart; i &lt; clipper.DisplayEnd; i++)</span></div>
<div class="line"><a name="l01782"></a><span class="lineno"> 1782</span>&#160;<span class="comment">//             ImGui::Text(&quot;line number %d&quot;, i);</span></div>
<div class="line"><a name="l01783"></a><span class="lineno"> 1783</span>&#160;<span class="comment">// - Step 0: the clipper let you process the first element, regardless of it being visible or not, so we can measure the element height (step skipped if we passed a known height as second arg to constructor).</span></div>
<div class="line"><a name="l01784"></a><span class="lineno"> 1784</span>&#160;<span class="comment">// - Step 1: the clipper infer height from first element, calculate the actual range of elements to display, and position the cursor before the first element.</span></div>
<div class="line"><a name="l01785"></a><span class="lineno"> 1785</span>&#160;<span class="comment">// - (Step 2: dummy step only required if an explicit items_height was passed to constructor or Begin() and user call Step(). Does nothing and switch to Step 3.)</span></div>
<div class="line"><a name="l01786"></a><span class="lineno"> 1786</span>&#160;<span class="comment">// - Step 3: the clipper validate that we have reached the expected Y position (corresponding to element DisplayEnd), advance the cursor to the end of the list and then returns &#39;false&#39; to end the loop.</span></div>
<div class="line"><a name="l01787"></a><span class="lineno"><a class="line" href="struct_im_gui_list_clipper.html"> 1787</a></span>&#160;<span class="keyword">struct </span><a class="code" href="struct_im_gui_list_clipper.html">ImGuiListClipper</a></div>
<div class="line"><a name="l01788"></a><span class="lineno"> 1788</span>&#160;{</div>
<div class="line"><a name="l01789"></a><span class="lineno"> 1789</span>&#160;    <span class="keywordtype">int</span>     DisplayStart, DisplayEnd;</div>
<div class="line"><a name="l01790"></a><span class="lineno"> 1790</span>&#160;    <span class="keywordtype">int</span>     ItemsCount;</div>
<div class="line"><a name="l01791"></a><span class="lineno"> 1791</span>&#160; </div>
<div class="line"><a name="l01792"></a><span class="lineno"> 1792</span>&#160;    <span class="comment">// [Internal]</span></div>
<div class="line"><a name="l01793"></a><span class="lineno"> 1793</span>&#160;    <span class="keywordtype">int</span>     StepNo;</div>
<div class="line"><a name="l01794"></a><span class="lineno"> 1794</span>&#160;    <span class="keywordtype">float</span>   ItemsHeight;</div>
<div class="line"><a name="l01795"></a><span class="lineno"> 1795</span>&#160;    <span class="keywordtype">float</span>   StartPosY;</div>
<div class="line"><a name="l01796"></a><span class="lineno"> 1796</span>&#160; </div>
<div class="line"><a name="l01797"></a><span class="lineno"> 1797</span>&#160;    <span class="comment">// items_count:  Use -1 to ignore (you can call Begin later). Use INT_MAX if you don&#39;t know how many items you have (in which case the cursor won&#39;t be advanced in the final step).</span></div>
<div class="line"><a name="l01798"></a><span class="lineno"> 1798</span>&#160;    <span class="comment">// items_height: Use -1.0f to be calculated automatically on first step. Otherwise pass in the distance between your items, typically GetTextLineHeightWithSpacing() or GetFrameHeightWithSpacing().</span></div>
<div class="line"><a name="l01799"></a><span class="lineno"> 1799</span>&#160;    <span class="comment">// If you don&#39;t specify an items_height, you NEED to call Step(). If you specify items_height you may call the old Begin()/End() api directly, but prefer calling Step().</span></div>
<div class="line"><a name="l01800"></a><span class="lineno"> 1800</span>&#160;    <a class="code" href="struct_im_gui_list_clipper.html">ImGuiListClipper</a>(<span class="keywordtype">int</span> items_count = -1, <span class="keywordtype">float</span> items_height = -1.0f)  { Begin(items_count, items_height); } <span class="comment">// NB: Begin() initialize every fields (as we allow user to call Begin/End multiple times on a same instance if they want).</span></div>

<div class="line"><a name="l01822"></a><span class="lineno"> 1822</span>&#160;<span class="preprocessor">#define IM_COL32(R,G,B,A)    (((ImU32)(A)&lt;&lt;IM_COL32_A_SHIFT) | ((ImU32)(B)&lt;&lt;IM_COL32_B_SHIFT) | ((ImU32)(G)&lt;&lt;IM_COL32_G_SHIFT) | ((ImU32)(R)&lt;&lt;IM_COL32_R_SHIFT))</span></div>

<div class="line"><a name="l01827"></a><span class="lineno"> 1827</span>&#160;<span class="comment">// Helper: ImColor() implicitly converts colors to either ImU32 (packed 4x1 byte) or ImVec4 (4x1 float)</span></div>
<div class="line"><a name="l01828"></a><span class="lineno"> 1828</span>&#160;<span class="comment">// Prefer using IM_COL32() macros if you want a guaranteed compile-time ImU32 for usage with ImDrawList API.</span></div>
<div class="line"><a name="l01829"></a><span class="lineno"> 1829</span>&#160;<span class="comment">// **Avoid storing ImColor! Store either u32 of ImVec4. This is not a full-featured color class. MAY OBSOLETE.</span></div>
<div class="line"><a name="l01830"></a><span class="lineno"> 1830</span>&#160;<span class="comment">// **None of the ImGui API are using ImColor directly but you can use it as a convenience to pass colors in either ImU32 or ImVec4 formats. Explicitly cast to ImU32 or ImVec4 if needed.</span></div>
<div class="line"><a name="l01831"></a><span class="lineno"><a class="line" href="struct_im_color.html"> 1831</a></span>&#160;<span class="keyword">struct </span><a class="code" href="struct_im_color.html">ImColor</a></div>
<div class="line"><a name="l01832"></a><span class="lineno"> 1832</span>&#160;{</div>
<div class="line"><a name="l01833"></a><span class="lineno"> 1833</span>&#160;    <a class="code" href="struct_im_vec4.html">ImVec4</a>              Value;</div>
<div class="line"><a name="l01834"></a><span class="lineno"> 1834</span>&#160; </div>
<div class="line"><a name="l01835"></a><span class="lineno"> 1835</span>&#160;    <a class="code" href="struct_im_color.html">ImColor</a>()                                                       { Value.x = Value.y = Value.z = Value.w = 0.0f; }</div>
<div class="line"><a name="l01836"></a><span class="lineno"> 1836</span>&#160;    <a class="code" href="struct_im_color.html">ImColor</a>(<span class="keywordtype">int</span> r, <span class="keywordtype">int</span> g, <span class="keywordtype">int</span> b, <span class="keywordtype">int</span> a = 255)                       { <span class="keywordtype">float</span> sc = 1.0f/255.0f; Value.x = (float)r * sc; Value.y = (float)g * sc; Value.z = (float)b * sc; Value.w = (float)a * sc; }</div>
<div class="line"><a name="l01837"></a><span class="lineno"> 1837</span>&#160;    <a class="code" href="struct_im_color.html">ImColor</a>(ImU32 rgba)                                             { <span class="keywordtype">float</span> sc = 1.0f/255.0f; Value.x = (float)((rgba&gt;&gt;IM_COL32_R_SHIFT)&amp;0xFF) * sc; Value.y = (float)((rgba&gt;&gt;IM_COL32_G_SHIFT)&amp;0xFF) * sc; Value.z = (float)((rgba&gt;&gt;IM_COL32_B_SHIFT)&amp;0xFF) * sc; Value.w = (float)((rgba&gt;&gt;IM_COL32_A_SHIFT)&amp;0xFF) * sc; }</div>
<div class="line"><a name="l01838"></a><span class="lineno"> 1838</span>&#160;    <a class="code" href="struct_im_color.html">ImColor</a>(<span class="keywordtype">float</span> r, <span class="keywordtype">float</span> g, <span class="keywordtype">float</span> b, <span class="keywordtype">float</span> a = 1.0f)              { Value.x = r; Value.y = g; Value.z = b; Value.w = a; }</div>
<div class="line"><a name="l01839"></a><span class="lineno"> 1839</span>&#160;    <a class="code" href="struct_im_color.html">ImColor</a>(<span class="keyword">const</span> <a class="code" href="struct_im_vec4.html">ImVec4</a>&amp; col)                                      { Value = col; }</div>
<div class="line"><a name="l01840"></a><span class="lineno"> 1840</span>&#160;    <span class="keyword">inline</span> <span class="keyword">operator</span> ImU32()<span class="keyword"> const                                   </span>{ <span class="keywordflow">return</span> ImGui::ColorConvertFloat4ToU32(Value); }</div>
<div class="line"><a name="l01841"></a><span class="lineno"> 1841</span>&#160;    <span class="keyword">inline</span> <span class="keyword">operator</span> <a class="code" href="struct_im_vec4.html">ImVec4</a>()<span class="keyword"> const                                  </span>{ <span class="keywordflow">return</span> Value; }</div>
<div class="line"><a name="l01842"></a><span class="lineno"> 1842</span>&#160; </div>
<div class="line"><a name="l01843"></a><span class="lineno"> 1843</span>&#160;    <span class="comment">// FIXME-OBSOLETE: May need to obsolete/cleanup those helpers.</span></div>
<div class="line"><a name="l01844"></a><span class="lineno"> 1844</span>&#160;    <span class="keyword">inline</span> <span class="keywordtype">void</span>    SetHSV(<span class="keywordtype">float</span> h, <span class="keywordtype">float</span> s, <span class="keywordtype">float</span> v, <span class="keywordtype">float</span> a = 1.0f){ ImGui::ColorConvertHSVtoRGB(h, s, v, Value.x, Value.y, Value.z); Value.w = a; }</div>
<div class="line"><a name="l01845"></a><span class="lineno"> 1845</span>&#160;    <span class="keyword">static</span> <a class="code" href="struct_im_color.html">ImColor</a> HSV(<span class="keywordtype">float</span> h, <span class="keywordtype">float</span> s, <span class="keywordtype">float</span> v, <span class="keywordtype">float</span> a = 1.0f)   { <span class="keywordtype">float</span> r,g,b; ImGui::ColorConvertHSVtoRGB(h, s, v, r, g, b); <span class="keywordflow">return</span> <a class="code" href="struct_im_color.html">ImColor</a>(r,g,b,a); }</div>
<div class="line"><a name="l01846"></a><span class="lineno"> 1846</span>&#160;};</div>

<div class="line"><a name="l01849"></a><span class="lineno"> 1849</span>&#160;<span class="comment">// Draw List API (ImDrawCmd, ImDrawIdx, ImDrawVert, ImDrawChannel, ImDrawListSplitter, ImDrawListFlags, ImDrawList, ImDrawData)</span></div>
<div class="line"><a name="l01850"></a><span class="lineno"> 1850</span>&#160;<span class="comment">// Hold a series of drawing commands. The user provides a renderer for ImDrawData which essentially contains an array of ImDrawList.</span></div>

<div class="line"><a name="l01853"></a><span class="lineno"> 1853</span>&#160;<span class="comment">// ImDrawCallback: Draw callbacks for advanced uses [configurable type: override in imconfig.h]</span></div>
<div class="line"><a name="l01854"></a><span class="lineno"> 1854</span>&#160;<span class="comment">// NB: You most likely do NOT need to use draw callbacks just to create your own widget or customized UI rendering,</span></div>
<div class="line"><a name="l01855"></a><span class="lineno"> 1855</span>&#160;<span class="comment">// you can poke into the draw list for that! Draw callback may be useful for example to:</span></div>
<div class="line"><a name="l01856"></a><span class="lineno"> 1856</span>&#160;<span class="comment">//  A) Change your GPU render state,</span></div>
<div class="line"><a name="l01857"></a><span class="lineno"> 1857</span>&#160;<span class="comment">//  B) render a complex 3D scene inside a UI element without an intermediate texture/render target, etc.</span></div>
<div class="line"><a name="l01858"></a><span class="lineno"> 1858</span>&#160;<span class="comment">// The expected behavior from your rendering function is &#39;if (cmd.UserCallback != NULL) { cmd.UserCallback(parent_list, cmd); } else { RenderTriangles() }&#39;</span></div>
<div class="line"><a name="l01859"></a><span class="lineno"> 1859</span>&#160;<span class="comment">// If you want to override the signature of ImDrawCallback, you can simply use e.g. &#39;#define ImDrawCallback MyDrawCallback&#39; (in imconfig.h) + update rendering back-end accordingly.</span></div>
<div class="line"><a name="l01860"></a><span class="lineno"> 1860</span>&#160;<span class="preprocessor">#ifndef ImDrawCallback</span></div>
<div class="line"><a name="l01861"></a><span class="lineno"> 1861</span>&#160;<span class="keyword">typedef</span> void (*ImDrawCallback)(<span class="keyword">const</span> <a class="code" href="struct_im_draw_list.html">ImDrawList</a>* parent_list, <span class="keyword">const</span> <a class="code" href="struct_im_draw_cmd.html">ImDrawCmd</a>* cmd);</div>
<div class="line"><a name="l01862"></a><span class="lineno"> 1862</span>&#160;<span class="preprocessor">#endif</span></div>
<div class="line"><a name="l01863"></a><span class="lineno"> 1863</span>&#160; </div>
<div class="line"><a name="l01864"></a><span class="lineno"> 1864</span>&#160;<span class="comment">// Special Draw callback value to request renderer back-end to reset the graphics/render state.</span></div>
<div class="line"><a name="l01865"></a><span class="lineno"> 1865</span>&#160;<span class="comment">// The renderer back-end needs to handle this special value, otherwise it will crash trying to call a function at this address.</span></div>
<div class="line"><a name="l01866"></a><span class="lineno"> 1866</span>&#160;<span class="comment">// This is useful for example if you submitted callbacks which you know have altered the render state and you want it to be restored.</span></div>
<div class="line"><a name="l01867"></a><span class="lineno"> 1867</span>&#160;<span class="comment">// It is not done by default because they are many perfectly useful way of altering render state for imgui contents (e.g. changing shader/blending settings before an Image call).</span></div>
<div class="line"><a name="l01868"></a><span class="lineno"> 1868</span>&#160;<span class="preprocessor">#define ImDrawCallback_ResetRenderState     (ImDrawCallback)(-1)</span></div>
<div class="line"><a name="l01869"></a><span class="lineno"> 1869</span>&#160; </div>
<div class="line"><a name="l01870"></a><span class="lineno"> 1870</span>&#160;<span class="comment">// Typically, 1 command = 1 GPU draw call (unless command is a callback)</span></div>
<div class="line"><a name="l01871"></a><span class="lineno"> 1871</span>&#160;<span class="comment">// Pre 1.71 back-ends will typically ignore the VtxOffset/IdxOffset fields. When &#39;io.BackendFlags &amp; ImGuiBackendFlags_RendererHasVtxOffset&#39;</span></div>
<div class="line"><a name="l01872"></a><span class="lineno"> 1872</span>&#160;<span class="comment">// is enabled, those fields allow us to render meshes larger than 64K vertices while keeping 16-bit indices.</span></div>
<div class="line"><a name="l01873"></a><span class="lineno"><a class="line" href="struct_im_draw_cmd.html"> 1873</a></span>&#160;<span class="keyword">struct </span><a class="code" href="struct_im_draw_cmd.html">ImDrawCmd</a></div>
<div class="line"><a name="l01874"></a><span class="lineno"> 1874</span>&#160;{</div>
<div class="line"><a name="l01875"></a><span class="lineno"> 1875</span>&#160;    <span class="keywordtype">unsigned</span> <span class="keywordtype">int</span>    ElemCount;              <span class="comment">// Number of indices (multiple of 3) to be rendered as triangles. Vertices are stored in the callee ImDrawList&#39;s vtx_buffer[] array, indices in idx_buffer[].</span></div>
<div class="line"><a name="l01876"></a><span class="lineno"> 1876</span>&#160;    <a class="code" href="struct_im_vec4.html">ImVec4</a>          ClipRect;               <span class="comment">// Clipping rectangle (x1, y1, x2, y2). Subtract ImDrawData-&gt;DisplayPos to get clipping rectangle in &quot;viewport&quot; coordinates</span></div>
<div class="line"><a name="l01877"></a><span class="lineno"> 1877</span>&#160;    ImTextureID     TextureId;              <span class="comment">// User-provided texture ID. Set by user in ImfontAtlas::SetTexID() for fonts or passed to Image*() functions. Ignore if never using images or multiple fonts atlas.</span></div>
<div class="line"><a name="l01878"></a><span class="lineno"> 1878</span>&#160;    <span class="keywordtype">unsigned</span> <span class="keywordtype">int</span>    VtxOffset;              <span class="comment">// Start offset in vertex buffer. Pre-1.71 or without ImGuiBackendFlags_RendererHasVtxOffset: always 0. With ImGuiBackendFlags_RendererHasVtxOffset: may be &gt;0 to support meshes larger than 64K vertices with 16-bit indices.</span></div>
<div class="line"><a name="l01879"></a><span class="lineno"> 1879</span>&#160;    <span class="keywordtype">unsigned</span> <span class="keywordtype">int</span>    IdxOffset;              <span class="comment">// Start offset in index buffer. Always equal to sum of ElemCount drawn so far.</span></div>
<div class="line"><a name="l01880"></a><span class="lineno"> 1880</span>&#160;    ImDrawCallback  UserCallback;           <span class="comment">// If != NULL, call the function instead of rendering the vertices. clip_rect and texture_id will be set normally.</span></div>
<div class="line"><a name="l01881"></a><span class="lineno"> 1881</span>&#160;    <span class="keywordtype">void</span>*           UserCallbackData;       <span class="comment">// The draw callback code can access this.</span></div>
<div class="line"><a name="l01882"></a><span class="lineno"> 1882</span>&#160; </div>
<div class="line"><a name="l01883"></a><span class="lineno"> 1883</span>&#160;    <a class="code" href="struct_im_draw_cmd.html">ImDrawCmd</a>() { ElemCount = 0; TextureId = (ImTextureID)NULL; VtxOffset = IdxOffset = 0;  UserCallback = NULL; UserCallbackData = NULL; }</div>
<div class="line"><a name="l01884"></a><span class="lineno"> 1884</span>&#160;};</div>
<div class="line"><a name="l01885"></a><span class="lineno"> 1885</span>&#160; </div>

<div class="line"><a name="l01887"></a><span class="lineno"> 1887</span>&#160;<span class="comment">// To allow large meshes with 16-bit indices: set &#39;io.BackendFlags |= ImGuiBackendFlags_RendererHasVtxOffset&#39; and handle ImDrawCmd::VtxOffset in the renderer back-end (recommended).</span></div>
<div class="line"><a name="l01888"></a><span class="lineno"> 1888</span>&#160;<span class="comment">// To use 32-bit indices: override with &#39;#define ImDrawIdx unsigned int&#39; in imconfig.h.</span></div>

<div class="line"><a name="l01894"></a><span class="lineno"> 1894</span>&#160;<span class="preprocessor">#ifndef IMGUI_OVERRIDE_DRAWVERT_STRUCT_LAYOUT</span></div>
<div class="line"><a name="l01895"></a><span class="lineno"><a class="line" href="struct_im_draw_vert.html"> 1895</a></span>&#160;<span class="keyword">struct </span><a class="code" href="struct_im_draw_vert.html">ImDrawVert</a></div>

<div class="line"><a name="l01901"></a><span class="lineno"> 1901</span>&#160;<span class="preprocessor">#else</span></div>
<div class="line"><a name="l01902"></a><span class="lineno"> 1902</span>&#160;<span class="comment">// You can override the vertex format layout by defining IMGUI_OVERRIDE_DRAWVERT_STRUCT_LAYOUT in imconfig.h</span></div>
<div class="line"><a name="l01903"></a><span class="lineno"> 1903</span>&#160;<span class="comment">// The code expect ImVec2 pos (8 bytes), ImVec2 uv (8 bytes), ImU32 col (4 bytes), but you can re-order them or add other fields as needed to simplify integration in your engine.</span></div>

<div class="line"><a name="l01905"></a><span class="lineno"> 1905</span>&#160;<span class="comment">// NOTE: IMGUI DOESN&#39;T CLEAR THE STRUCTURE AND DOESN&#39;T CALL A CONSTRUCTOR SO ANY CUSTOM FIELD WILL BE UNINITIALIZED. <div class="line"><a name="l01906"></a><span class="lineno"> 1906</span>&#160;IMGUI_OVERRIDE_DRAWVERT_STRUCT_LAYOUT;</div>

<div class="line"><a name="l01933"></a><span class="lineno"> 1933</span>&#160;<span class="keyword">enum</span> ImDrawCornerFlags_</div>

<div class="line"><a name="l01936"></a><span class="lineno"> 1936</span>&#160;    ImDrawCornerFlags_TopLeft   = 1 &lt;&lt; 0, <span class="comment">// 0x1</span></div>

<div class="line"><a name="l02139"></a><span class="lineno"> 2139</span>&#160;    <span class="keyword">inline</span> <span class="keywordtype">bool</span>     GetBit(<span class="keywordtype">size_t</span> n)<span class="keyword"> const  </span>{ <span class="keywordtype">int</span> off = (int)(n &gt;&gt; 5); ImU32 mask = 1u &lt;&lt; (n &amp; 31); <span class="keywordflow">return</span> (UsedChars[off] &amp; mask) != 0; }  <span class="comment">// Get bit n in the array</span></div>
<div class="line"><a name="l02140"></a><span class="lineno"> 2140</span>&#160;    <span class="keyword">inline</span> <span class="keywordtype">void</span>     SetBit(<span class="keywordtype">size_t</span> n)        { <span class="keywordtype">int</span> off = (int)(n &gt;&gt; 5); ImU32 mask = 1u &lt;&lt; (n &amp; 31); UsedChars[off] |= mask; }               <span class="comment">// Set bit n in the array</span></div>
<div class="line"><a name="l02141"></a><span class="lineno"> 2141</span>&#160;    <span class="keyword">inline</span> <span class="keywordtype">void</span>     AddChar(ImWchar c)      { SetBit(c); }                      <span class="comment">// Add character</span></div>

<div class="line"><a name="l02166"></a><span class="lineno"> 2166</span>&#160; </div>
<div class="line"><a name="l02167"></a><span class="lineno"> 2167</span>&#160;<span class="comment">// Load and rasterize multiple TTF/OTF fonts into a same texture. The font atlas will build a single texture holding:</span></div>
<div class="line"><a name="l02168"></a><span class="lineno"> 2168</span>&#160;<span class="comment">//  - One or more fonts.</span></div>
<div class="line"><a name="l02169"></a><span class="lineno"> 2169</span>&#160;<span class="comment">//  - Custom graphics data needed to render the shapes needed by Dear ImGui.</span></div>
<div class="line"><a name="l02170"></a><span class="lineno"> 2170</span>&#160;<span class="comment">//  - Mouse cursor shapes for software cursor rendering (unless setting &#39;Flags |= ImFontAtlasFlags_NoMouseCursors&#39; in the font atlas).</span></div>
<div class="line"><a name="l02171"></a><span class="lineno"> 2171</span>&#160;<span class="comment">// It is the user-code responsibility to setup/build the atlas, then upload the pixel data into a texture accessible by your graphics api.</span></div>
<div class="line"><a name="l02172"></a><span class="lineno"> 2172</span>&#160;<span class="comment">//  - Optionally, call any of the AddFont*** functions. If you don&#39;t call any, the default font embedded in the code will be loaded for you.</span></div>
<div class="line"><a name="l02173"></a><span class="lineno"> 2173</span>&#160;<span class="comment">//  - Call GetTexDataAsAlpha8() or GetTexDataAsRGBA32() to build and retrieve pixels data.</span></div>
<div class="line"><a name="l02174"></a><span class="lineno"> 2174</span>&#160;<span class="comment">//  - Upload the pixels data into a texture within your graphics system (see imgui_impl_xxxx.cpp examples)</span></div>
<div class="line"><a name="l02175"></a><span class="lineno"> 2175</span>&#160;<span class="comment">//  - Call SetTexID(my_tex_id); and pass the pointer/identifier to your texture in a format natural to your graphics API.</span></div>
<div class="line"><a name="l02176"></a><span class="lineno"> 2176</span>&#160;<span class="comment">//    This value will be passed back to you during rendering to identify the texture. Read FAQ entry about ImTextureID for more details.</span></div>
<div class="line"><a name="l02177"></a><span class="lineno"> 2177</span>&#160;<span class="comment">// Common pitfalls:</span></div>
<div class="line"><a name="l02178"></a><span class="lineno"> 2178</span>&#160;<span class="comment">// - If you pass a &#39;glyph_ranges&#39; array to AddFont*** functions, you need to make sure that your array persist up until the</span></div>
<div class="line"><a name="l02179"></a><span class="lineno"> 2179</span>&#160;<span class="comment">//   atlas is build (when calling GetTexData*** or Build()). We only copy the pointer, not the data.</span></div>
<div class="line"><a name="l02180"></a><span class="lineno"> 2180</span>&#160;<span class="comment">// - Important: By default, AddFontFromMemoryTTF() takes ownership of the data. Even though we are not writing to it, we will free the pointer on destruction.</span></div>
<div class="line"><a name="l02181"></a><span class="lineno"> 2181</span>&#160;<span class="comment">//   You can set font_cfg-&gt;FontDataOwnedByAtlas=false to keep ownership of your data and it won&#39;t be freed,</span></div>
<div class="line"><a name="l02182"></a><span class="lineno"> 2182</span>&#160;<span class="comment">// - Even though many functions are suffixed with &quot;TTF&quot;, OTF data is supported just as well.</span></div>
<div class="line"><a name="l02183"></a><span class="lineno"> 2183</span>&#160;<span class="comment">// - This is an old API and it is currently awkward for those and and various other reasons! We will address them in the future!</span></div>

<div class="line"><a name="l02202"></a><span class="lineno"> 2202</span>&#160;    <span class="comment">// Building in RGBA32 format is provided for convenience and compatibility, but note that unless you manually manipulate or copy color data into</span></div>

<div class="line"><a name="l00424"></a><span class="lineno">  424</span>&#160;    T*      alloc_chunk(<span class="keywordtype">size_t</span> sz)      { <span class="keywordtype">size_t</span> HDR_SZ = 4; sz = ((HDR_SZ + sz) + 3u) &amp; ~3u; <span class="keywordtype">int</span> off = Buf.Size; Buf.resize(off + (<span class="keywordtype">int</span>)sz); ((<span class="keywordtype">int</span>*)(<span class="keywordtype">void</span>*)(Buf.Data + off))[0] = (int)sz; <span class="keywordflow">return</span> (T*)(<span class="keywordtype">void</span>*)(Buf.Data + off + (<span class="keywordtype">int</span>)HDR_SZ); }</div>
<div class="line"><a name="l00425"></a><span class="lineno">  425</span>&#160;    T*      begin()                     { <span class="keywordtype">size_t</span> HDR_SZ = 4; <span class="keywordflow">if</span> (!Buf.Data) <span class="keywordflow">return</span> NULL; <span class="keywordflow">return</span> (T*)(<span class="keywordtype">void</span>*)(Buf.Data + HDR_SZ); }</div>
<div class="line"><a name="l00426"></a><span class="lineno">  426</span>&#160;    T*      next_chunk(T* p)            { <span class="keywordtype">size_t</span> HDR_SZ = 4; IM_ASSERT(p &gt;= begin() &amp;&amp; p &lt; end()); p = (T*)(<span class="keywordtype">void</span>*)((<span class="keywordtype">char</span>*)(<span class="keywordtype">void</span>*)p + chunk_size(p)); <span class="keywordflow">if</span> (p == (T*)(<span class="keywordtype">void</span>*)((<span class="keywordtype">char</span>*)end() + HDR_SZ)) <span class="keywordflow">return</span> (T*)0; IM_ASSERT(p &lt; end()); <span class="keywordflow">return</span> p; }</div>
<div class="line"><a name="l00427"></a><span class="lineno">  427</span>&#160;    <span class="keywordtype">int</span>     chunk_size(<span class="keyword">const</span> T* p)      { <span class="keywordflow">return</span> ((<span class="keyword">const</span> <span class="keywordtype">int</span>*)p)[-1]; }</div>
<div class="line"><a name="l00428"></a><span class="lineno">  428</span>&#160;    T*      end()                       { <span class="keywordflow">return</span> (T*)(<span class="keywordtype">void</span>*)(Buf.Data + Buf.Size); }</div>
<div class="line"><a name="l00429"></a><span class="lineno">  429</span>&#160;    <span class="keywordtype">int</span>     offset_from_ptr(<span class="keyword">const</span> T* p) { IM_ASSERT(p &gt;= begin() &amp;&amp; p &lt; end()); <span class="keyword">const</span> ptrdiff_t off = (<span class="keyword">const</span> <span class="keywordtype">char</span>*)p - Buf.Data; return (<span class="keywordtype">int</span>)off; }</div>

<div class="line"><a name="l00705"></a><span class="lineno">  705</span>&#160;    <span class="keywordtype">void</span>        Add(<span class="keyword">const</span> <a class="code" href="struct_im_vec2.html">ImVec2</a>&amp; p)                { <span class="keywordflow">if</span> (Min.x &gt; p.x)     Min.x = p.x;     <span class="keywordflow">if</span> (Min.y &gt; p.y)     Min.y = p.y;     <span class="keywordflow">if</span> (Max.x &lt; p.x)     Max.x = p.x;     <span class="keywordflow">if</span> (Max.y &lt; p.y)     Max.y = p.y; }</div>
<div class="line"><a name="l00706"></a><span class="lineno">  706</span>&#160;    <span class="keywordtype">void</span>        Add(<span class="keyword">const</span> <a class="code" href="struct_im_rect.html">ImRect</a>&amp; r)                { <span class="keywordflow">if</span> (Min.x &gt; r.Min.x) Min.x = r.Min.x; <span class="keywordflow">if</span> (Min.y &gt; r.Min.y) Min.y = r.Min.y; <span class="keywordflow">if</span> (Max.x &lt; r.Max.x) Max.x = r.Max.x; <span class="keywordflow">if</span> (Max.y &lt; r.Max.y) Max.y = r.Max.y; }</div>

<div class="line"><a name="l00110"></a><span class="lineno">  110</span>&#160;<span class="comment">// available.</span></div>
<div class="line"><a name="l00111"></a><span class="lineno">  111</span>&#160;<span class="comment">//</span></div>

<div class="line"><a name="l00230"></a><span class="lineno">  230</span>&#160;STBRP_DEF <span class="keywordtype">void</span> stbrp_setup_heuristic(<a class="code" href="structstbrp__context.html">stbrp_context</a> *context, <span class="keywordtype">int</span> heuristic)</div>
<div class="line"><a name="l00231"></a><span class="lineno">  231</span>&#160;{</div>
<div class="line"><a name="l00232"></a><span class="lineno">  232</span>&#160;   <span class="keywordflow">switch</span> (context-&gt;init_mode) {</div>

<div class="line"><a name="l00234"></a><span class="lineno">  234</span>&#160;         STBRP_ASSERT(heuristic == STBRP_HEURISTIC_Skyline_BL_sortHeight || heuristic == STBRP_HEURISTIC_Skyline_BF_sortHeight);</div>

<div class="line"><a name="l00242"></a><span class="lineno">  242</span>&#160;STBRP_DEF <span class="keywordtype">void</span> stbrp_setup_allow_out_of_mem(<a class="code" href="structstbrp__context.html">stbrp_context</a> *context, <span class="keywordtype">int</span> allow_out_of_mem)</div>
<div class="line"><a name="l00243"></a><span class="lineno">  243</span>&#160;{</div>
<div class="line"><a name="l00244"></a><span class="lineno">  244</span>&#160;   <span class="keywordflow">if</span> (allow_out_of_mem)</div>
<div class="line"><a name="l00245"></a><span class="lineno">  245</span>&#160;      <span class="comment">// if it&#39;s ok to run out of memory, then don&#39;t bother aligning them;</span></div>
<div class="line"><a name="l00246"></a><span class="lineno">  246</span>&#160;      <span class="comment">// this gives better packing, but may fail due to OOM (even though</span></div>
<div class="line"><a name="l00247"></a><span class="lineno">  247</span>&#160;      <span class="comment">// the rectangles easily fit). @TODO a smarter approach would be to only</span></div>
<div class="line"><a name="l00248"></a><span class="lineno">  248</span>&#160;      <span class="comment">// quantize once we&#39;ve hit OOM, then we could get rid of this parameter.</span></div>
<div class="line"><a name="l00249"></a><span class="lineno">  249</span>&#160;      context-&gt;align = 1;</div>
<div class="line"><a name="l00250"></a><span class="lineno">  250</span>&#160;   <span class="keywordflow">else</span> {</div>
<div class="line"><a name="l00251"></a><span class="lineno">  251</span>&#160;      <span class="comment">// if it&#39;s not ok to run out of memory, then quantize the widths</span></div>
<div class="line"><a name="l00252"></a><span class="lineno">  252</span>&#160;      <span class="comment">// so that num_nodes is always enough nodes.</span></div>
<div class="line"><a name="l00253"></a><span class="lineno">  253</span>&#160;      <span class="comment">//</span></div>
<div class="line"><a name="l00254"></a><span class="lineno">  254</span>&#160;      <span class="comment">// I.e. num_nodes * align &gt;= width</span></div>
<div class="line"><a name="l00255"></a><span class="lineno">  255</span>&#160;      <span class="comment">//                  align &gt;= width / num_nodes</span></div>
<div class="line"><a name="l00256"></a><span class="lineno">  256</span>&#160;      <span class="comment">//                  align = ceil(width/num_nodes)</span></div>
<div class="line"><a name="l00257"></a><span class="lineno">  257</span>&#160; </div>
<div class="line"><a name="l00258"></a><span class="lineno">  258</span>&#160;      context-&gt;align = (context-&gt;width + context-&gt;num_nodes-1) / context-&gt;num_nodes;</div>
<div class="line"><a name="l00259"></a><span class="lineno">  259</span>&#160;   }</div>
<div class="line"><a name="l00260"></a><span class="lineno">  260</span>&#160;}</div>

<div class="line"><a name="l00294"></a><span class="lineno">  294</span>&#160;<span class="comment">// find minimum y position if it starts at x1</span></div>
<div class="line"><a name="l00295"></a><span class="lineno">  295</span>&#160;<span class="keyword">static</span> <span class="keywordtype">int</span> stbrp__skyline_find_min_y(<a class="code" href="structstbrp__context.html">stbrp_context</a> *c, <a class="code" href="structstbrp__node.html">stbrp_node</a> *first, <span class="keywordtype">int</span> x0, <span class="keywordtype">int</span> width, <span class="keywordtype">int</span> *pwaste)</div>

<div class="line"><a name="l00297"></a><span class="lineno">  297</span>&#160;   <a class="code" href="structstbrp__node.html">stbrp_node</a> *node = first;</div>
<div class="line"><a name="l00298"></a><span class="lineno">  298</span>&#160;   <span class="keywordtype">int</span> x1 = x0 + width;</div>
<div class="line"><a name="l00299"></a><span class="lineno">  299</span>&#160;   <span class="keywordtype">int</span> min_y, visited_width, waste_area;</div>

<div class="line"><a name="l00306"></a><span class="lineno">  306</span>&#160;   <span class="comment">// skip in case we&#39;re past the node</span></div>
<div class="line"><a name="l00307"></a><span class="lineno">  307</span>&#160;   <span class="keywordflow">while</span> (node-&gt;next-&gt;x &lt;= x0)</div>

<div class="line"><a name="l00309"></a><span class="lineno">  309</span>&#160;<span class="preprocessor">   #else</span></div>

<div class="line"><a name="l00316"></a><span class="lineno">  316</span>&#160;   waste_area = 0;</div>
<div class="line"><a name="l00317"></a><span class="lineno">  317</span>&#160;   visited_width = 0;</div>
<div class="line"><a name="l00318"></a><span class="lineno">  318</span>&#160;   <span class="keywordflow">while</span> (node-&gt;x &lt; x1) {</div>
<div class="line"><a name="l00319"></a><span class="lineno">  319</span>&#160;      <span class="keywordflow">if</span> (node-&gt;y &gt; min_y) {</div>
<div class="line"><a name="l00320"></a><span class="lineno">  320</span>&#160;         <span class="comment">// raise min_y higher.</span></div>
<div class="line"><a name="l00321"></a><span class="lineno">  321</span>&#160;         <span class="comment">// we&#39;ve accounted for all waste up to min_y,</span></div>
<div class="line"><a name="l00322"></a><span class="lineno">  322</span>&#160;         <span class="comment">// but we&#39;ll now add more waste for everything we&#39;ve visted</span></div>
<div class="line"><a name="l00323"></a><span class="lineno">  323</span>&#160;         waste_area += visited_width * (node-&gt;y - min_y);</div>

<div class="line"><a name="l00325"></a><span class="lineno">  325</span>&#160;         <span class="comment">// the first time through, visited_width might be reduced</span></div>

<div class="line"><a name="l00327"></a><span class="lineno">  327</span>&#160;            visited_width += node-&gt;next-&gt;x - x0;</div>
<div class="line"><a name="l00328"></a><span class="lineno">  328</span>&#160;         <span class="keywordflow">else</span></div>
<div class="line"><a name="l00329"></a><span class="lineno">  329</span>&#160;            visited_width += node-&gt;next-&gt;x - node-&gt;x;</div>
<div class="line"><a name="l00330"></a><span class="lineno">  330</span>&#160;      } <span class="keywordflow">else</span> {</div>
<div class="line"><a name="l00331"></a><span class="lineno">  331</span>&#160;         <span class="comment">// add waste area</span></div>
<div class="line"><a name="l00332"></a><span class="lineno">  332</span>&#160;         <span class="keywordtype">int</span> under_width = node-&gt;next-&gt;x - node-&gt;x;</div>
<div class="line"><a name="l00333"></a><span class="lineno">  333</span>&#160;         <span class="keywordflow">if</span> (under_width + visited_width &gt; width)</div>
<div class="line"><a name="l00334"></a><span class="lineno">  334</span>&#160;            under_width = width - visited_width;</div>
<div class="line"><a name="l00335"></a><span class="lineno">  335</span>&#160;         waste_area += under_width * (min_y - node-&gt;y);</div>
<div class="line"><a name="l00336"></a><span class="lineno">  336</span>&#160;         visited_width += under_width;</div>
<div class="line"><a name="l00337"></a><span class="lineno">  337</span>&#160;      }</div>
<div class="line"><a name="l00338"></a><span class="lineno">  338</span>&#160;      node = node-&gt;next;</div>
<div class="line"><a name="l00339"></a><span class="lineno">  339</span>&#160;   }</div>
<div class="line"><a name="l00340"></a><span class="lineno">  340</span>&#160; </div>
<div class="line"><a name="l00341"></a><span class="lineno">  341</span>&#160;   *pwaste = waste_area;</div>
<div class="line"><a name="l00342"></a><span class="lineno">  342</span>&#160;   <span class="keywordflow">return</span> min_y;</div>
<div class="line"><a name="l00343"></a><span class="lineno">  343</span>&#160;}</div>

<div class="line"><a name="l00345"></a><span class="lineno">  345</span>&#160;<span class="keyword">typedef</span> <span class="keyword">struct</span></div>
<div class="line"><a name="l00346"></a><span class="lineno">  346</span>&#160;{</div>

<div class="line"><a name="l00351"></a><span class="lineno">  351</span>&#160;<span class="keyword">static</span> stbrp__findresult stbrp__skyline_find_best_pos(<a class="code" href="structstbrp__context.html">stbrp_context</a> *c, <span class="keywordtype">int</span> width, <span class="keywordtype">int</span> height)</div>
<div class="line"><a name="l00352"></a><span class="lineno">  352</span>&#160;{</div>
<div class="line"><a name="l00353"></a><span class="lineno">  353</span>&#160;   <span class="keywordtype">int</span> best_waste = (1&lt;&lt;30), best_x, best_y = (1 &lt;&lt; 30);</div>
<div class="line"><a name="l00354"></a><span class="lineno">  354</span>&#160;   stbrp__findresult fr;</div>
<div class="line"><a name="l00355"></a><span class="lineno">  355</span>&#160;   <a class="code" href="structstbrp__node.html">stbrp_node</a> **prev, *node, *tail, **best = NULL;</div>

<div class="line"><a name="l00358"></a><span class="lineno">  358</span>&#160;   width = (width + c-&gt;align - 1);</div>
<div class="line"><a name="l00359"></a><span class="lineno">  359</span>&#160;   width -= width % c-&gt;align;</div>
<div class="line"><a name="l00360"></a><span class="lineno">  360</span>&#160;   STBRP_ASSERT(width % c-&gt;align == 0);</div>

<div class="line"><a name="l00363"></a><span class="lineno">  363</span>&#160;   <span class="keywordflow">if</span> (width &gt; c-&gt;width || height &gt; c-&gt;height) {</div>

<div class="line"><a name="l00365"></a><span class="lineno">  365</span>&#160;      fr.x = fr.y = 0;</div>

<div class="line"><a name="l00373"></a><span class="lineno">  373</span>&#160;      y = stbrp__skyline_find_min_y(c, node, node-&gt;x, width, &amp;waste);</div>
<div class="line"><a name="l00374"></a><span class="lineno">  374</span>&#160;      <span class="keywordflow">if</span> (c-&gt;heuristic == STBRP_HEURISTIC_Skyline_BL_sortHeight) { <span class="comment">// actually just want to test BL</span></div>
<div class="line"><a name="l00375"></a><span class="lineno">  375</span>&#160;         <span class="comment">// bottom left</span></div>
<div class="line"><a name="l00376"></a><span class="lineno">  376</span>&#160;         <span class="keywordflow">if</span> (y &lt; best_y) {</div>

<div class="line"><a name="l00062"></a><span class="lineno">   62</span>&#160;<span class="comment">//   Bugfixes:</span></div>
<div class="line"><a name="l00063"></a><span class="lineno">   63</span>&#160;<span class="comment">//      Scott Graham</span></div>
<div class="line"><a name="l00064"></a><span class="lineno">   64</span>&#160;<span class="comment">//      Daniel Keller</span></div>
<div class="line"><a name="l00065"></a><span class="lineno">   65</span>&#160;<span class="comment">//      Omar Cornut</span></div>
<div class="line"><a name="l00066"></a><span class="lineno">   66</span>&#160;<span class="comment">//      Dan Thompson</span></div>
<div class="line"><a name="l00067"></a><span class="lineno">   67</span>&#160;<span class="comment">//</span></div>
<div class="line"><a name="l00068"></a><span class="lineno">   68</span>&#160;<span class="comment">// USAGE</span></div>
<div class="line"><a name="l00069"></a><span class="lineno">   69</span>&#160;<span class="comment">//</span></div>
<div class="line"><a name="l00070"></a><span class="lineno">   70</span>&#160;<span class="comment">// This file behaves differently depending on what symbols you define</span></div>
<div class="line"><a name="l00071"></a><span class="lineno">   71</span>&#160;<span class="comment">// before including it.</span></div>
<div class="line"><a name="l00072"></a><span class="lineno">   72</span>&#160;<span class="comment">//</span></div>
<div class="line"><a name="l00073"></a><span class="lineno">   73</span>&#160;<span class="comment">//</span></div>
<div class="line"><a name="l00074"></a><span class="lineno">   74</span>&#160;<span class="comment">// Header-file mode:</span></div>
<div class="line"><a name="l00075"></a><span class="lineno">   75</span>&#160;<span class="comment">//</span></div>
<div class="line"><a name="l00076"></a><span class="lineno">   76</span>&#160;<span class="comment">//   If you do not define STB_TEXTEDIT_IMPLEMENTATION before including this,</span></div>
<div class="line"><a name="l00077"></a><span class="lineno">   77</span>&#160;<span class="comment">//   it will operate in &quot;header file&quot; mode. In this mode, it declares a</span></div>
<div class="line"><a name="l00078"></a><span class="lineno">   78</span>&#160;<span class="comment">//   single public symbol, STB_TexteditState, which encapsulates the current</span></div>
<div class="line"><a name="l00079"></a><span class="lineno">   79</span>&#160;<span class="comment">//   state of a text widget (except for the string, which you will store</span></div>
<div class="line"><a name="l00080"></a><span class="lineno">   80</span>&#160;<span class="comment">//   separately).</span></div>
<div class="line"><a name="l00081"></a><span class="lineno">   81</span>&#160;<span class="comment">//</span></div>
<div class="line"><a name="l00082"></a><span class="lineno">   82</span>&#160;<span class="comment">//   To compile in this mode, you must define STB_TEXTEDIT_CHARTYPE to a</span></div>
<div class="line"><a name="l00083"></a><span class="lineno">   83</span>&#160;<span class="comment">//   primitive type that defines a single character (e.g. char, wchar_t, etc).</span></div>
<div class="line"><a name="l00084"></a><span class="lineno">   84</span>&#160;<span class="comment">//</span></div>
<div class="line"><a name="l00085"></a><span class="lineno">   85</span>&#160;<span class="comment">//   To save space or increase undo-ability, you can optionally define the</span></div>
<div class="line"><a name="l00086"></a><span class="lineno">   86</span>&#160;<span class="comment">//   following things that are used by the undo system:</span></div>
<div class="line"><a name="l00087"></a><span class="lineno">   87</span>&#160;<span class="comment">//</span></div>
<div class="line"><a name="l00088"></a><span class="lineno">   88</span>&#160;<span class="comment">//      STB_TEXTEDIT_POSITIONTYPE         small int type encoding a valid cursor position</span></div>
<div class="line"><a name="l00089"></a><span class="lineno">   89</span>&#160;<span class="comment">//      STB_TEXTEDIT_UNDOSTATECOUNT       the number of undo states to allow</span></div>
<div class="line"><a name="l00090"></a><span class="lineno">   90</span>&#160;<span class="comment">//      STB_TEXTEDIT_UNDOCHARCOUNT        the number of characters to store in the undo buffer</span></div>
<div class="line"><a name="l00091"></a><span class="lineno">   91</span>&#160;<span class="comment">//</span></div>
<div class="line"><a name="l00092"></a><span class="lineno">   92</span>&#160;<span class="comment">//   If you don&#39;t define these, they are set to permissive types and</span></div>
<div class="line"><a name="l00093"></a><span class="lineno">   93</span>&#160;<span class="comment">//   moderate sizes. The undo system does no memory allocations, so</span></div>
<div class="line"><a name="l00094"></a><span class="lineno">   94</span>&#160;<span class="comment">//   it grows STB_TexteditState by the worst-case storage which is (in bytes):</span></div>
<div class="line"><a name="l00095"></a><span class="lineno">   95</span>&#160;<span class="comment">//</span></div>
<div class="line"><a name="l00096"></a><span class="lineno">   96</span>&#160;<span class="comment">//        [4 + 3 * sizeof(STB_TEXTEDIT_POSITIONTYPE)] * STB_TEXTEDIT_UNDOSTATE_COUNT</span></div>
<div class="line"><a name="l00097"></a><span class="lineno">   97</span>&#160;<span class="comment">//      +          sizeof(STB_TEXTEDIT_CHARTYPE)      * STB_TEXTEDIT_UNDOCHAR_COUNT</span></div>
<div class="line"><a name="l00098"></a><span class="lineno">   98</span>&#160;<span class="comment">//</span></div>
<div class="line"><a name="l00099"></a><span class="lineno">   99</span>&#160;<span class="comment">//</span></div>
<div class="line"><a name="l00100"></a><span class="lineno">  100</span>&#160;<span class="comment">// Implementation mode:</span></div>
<div class="line"><a name="l00101"></a><span class="lineno">  101</span>&#160;<span class="comment">//</span></div>
<div class="line"><a name="l00102"></a><span class="lineno">  102</span>&#160;<span class="comment">//   If you define STB_TEXTEDIT_IMPLEMENTATION before including this, it</span></div>
<div class="line"><a name="l00103"></a><span class="lineno">  103</span>&#160;<span class="comment">//   will compile the implementation of the text edit widget, depending</span></div>
<div class="line"><a name="l00104"></a><span class="lineno">  104</span>&#160;<span class="comment">//   on a large number of symbols which must be defined before the include.</span></div>
<div class="line"><a name="l00105"></a><span class="lineno">  105</span>&#160;<span class="comment">//</span></div>
<div class="line"><a name="l00106"></a><span class="lineno">  106</span>&#160;<span class="comment">//   The implementation is defined only as static functions. You will then</span></div>
<div class="line"><a name="l00107"></a><span class="lineno">  107</span>&#160;<span class="comment">//   need to provide your own APIs in the same file which will access the</span></div>
<div class="line"><a name="l00108"></a><span class="lineno">  108</span>&#160;<span class="comment">//   static functions.</span></div>
<div class="line"><a name="l00109"></a><span class="lineno">  109</span>&#160;<span class="comment">//</span></div>
<div class="line"><a name="l00110"></a><span class="lineno">  110</span>&#160;<span class="comment">//   The basic concept is that you provide a &quot;string&quot; object which</span></div>
<div class="line"><a name="l00111"></a><span class="lineno">  111</span>&#160;<span class="comment">//   behaves like an array of characters. stb_textedit uses indices to</span></div>
<div class="line"><a name="l00112"></a><span class="lineno">  112</span>&#160;<span class="comment">//   refer to positions in the string, implicitly representing positions</span></div>
<div class="line"><a name="l00113"></a><span class="lineno">  113</span>&#160;<span class="comment">//   in the displayed textedit. This is true for both plain text and</span></div>
<div class="line"><a name="l00114"></a><span class="lineno">  114</span>&#160;<span class="comment">//   rich text; even with rich text stb_truetype interacts with your</span></div>
<div class="line"><a name="l00115"></a><span class="lineno">  115</span>&#160;<span class="comment">//   code as if there was an array of all the displayed characters.</span></div>
<div class="line"><a name="l00116"></a><span class="lineno">  116</span>&#160;<span class="comment">//</span></div>
<div class="line"><a name="l00117"></a><span class="lineno">  117</span>&#160;<span class="comment">// Symbols that must be the same in header-file and implementation mode:</span></div>
<div class="line"><a name="l00118"></a><span class="lineno">  118</span>&#160;<span class="comment">//</span></div>
<div class="line"><a name="l00119"></a><span class="lineno">  119</span>&#160;<span class="comment">//     STB_TEXTEDIT_CHARTYPE             the character type</span></div>
<div class="line"><a name="l00120"></a><span class="lineno">  120</span>&#160;<span class="comment">//     STB_TEXTEDIT_POSITIONTYPE         small type that is a valid cursor position</span></div>
<div class="line"><a name="l00121"></a><span class="lineno">  121</span>&#160;<span class="comment">//     STB_TEXTEDIT_UNDOSTATECOUNT       the number of undo states to allow</span></div>
<div class="line"><a name="l00122"></a><span class="lineno">  122</span>&#160;<span class="comment">//     STB_TEXTEDIT_UNDOCHARCOUNT        the number of characters to store in the undo buffer</span></div>
<div class="line"><a name="l00123"></a><span class="lineno">  123</span>&#160;<span class="comment">//</span></div>
<div class="line"><a name="l00124"></a><span class="lineno">  124</span>&#160;<span class="comment">// Symbols you must define for implementation mode:</span></div>
<div class="line"><a name="l00125"></a><span class="lineno">  125</span>&#160;<span class="comment">//</span></div>
<div class="line"><a name="l00126"></a><span class="lineno">  126</span>&#160;<span class="comment">//    STB_TEXTEDIT_STRING               the type of object representing a string being edited,</span></div>
<div class="line"><a name="l00127"></a><span class="lineno">  127</span>&#160;<span class="comment">//                                      typically this is a wrapper object with other data you need</span></div>
<div class="line"><a name="l00128"></a><span class="lineno">  128</span>&#160;<span class="comment">//</span></div>
<div class="line"><a name="l00129"></a><span class="lineno">  129</span>&#160;<span class="comment">//    STB_TEXTEDIT_STRINGLEN(obj)       the length of the string (ideally O(1))</span></div>
<div class="line"><a name="l00130"></a><span class="lineno">  130</span>&#160;<span class="comment">//    STB_TEXTEDIT_LAYOUTROW(&amp;r,obj,n)  returns the results of laying out a line of characters</span></div>
<div class="line"><a name="l00131"></a><span class="lineno">  131</span>&#160;<span class="comment">//                                        starting from character #n (see discussion below)</span></div>
<div class="line"><a name="l00132"></a><span class="lineno">  132</span>&#160;<span class="comment">//    STB_TEXTEDIT_GETWIDTH(obj,n,i)    returns the pixel delta from the xpos of the i&#39;th character</span></div>
<div class="line"><a name="l00133"></a><span class="lineno">  133</span>&#160;<span class="comment">//                                        to the xpos of the i+1&#39;th char for a line of characters</span></div>
<div class="line"><a name="l00134"></a><span class="lineno">  134</span>&#160;<span class="comment">//                                        starting at character #n (i.e. accounts for kerning</span></div>
<div class="line"><a name="l00135"></a><span class="lineno">  135</span>&#160;<span class="comment">//                                        with previous char)</span></div>
<div class="line"><a name="l00136"></a><span class="lineno">  136</span>&#160;<span class="comment">//    STB_TEXTEDIT_KEYTOTEXT(k)         maps a keyboard input to an insertable character</span></div>
<div class="line"><a name="l00137"></a><span class="lineno">  137</span>&#160;<span class="comment">//                                        (return type is int, -1 means not valid to insert)</span></div>
<div class="line"><a name="l00138"></a><span class="lineno">  138</span>&#160;<span class="comment">//    STB_TEXTEDIT_GETCHAR(obj,i)       returns the i&#39;th character of obj, 0-based</span></div>
<div class="line"><a name="l00139"></a><span class="lineno">  139</span>&#160;<span class="comment">//    STB_TEXTEDIT_NEWLINE              the character returned by _GETCHAR() we recognize</span></div>
<div class="line"><a name="l00140"></a><span class="lineno">  140</span>&#160;<span class="comment">//                                        as manually wordwrapping for end-of-line positioning</span></div>
<div class="line"><a name="l00141"></a><span class="lineno">  141</span>&#160;<span class="comment">//</span></div>
<div class="line"><a name="l00142"></a><span class="lineno">  142</span>&#160;<span class="comment">//    STB_TEXTEDIT_DELETECHARS(obj,i,n)      delete n characters starting at i</span></div>
<div class="line"><a name="l00143"></a><span class="lineno">  143</span>&#160;<span class="comment">//    STB_TEXTEDIT_INSERTCHARS(obj,i,c*,n)   insert n characters at i (pointed to by STB_TEXTEDIT_CHARTYPE*)</span></div>
<div class="line"><a name="l00144"></a><span class="lineno">  144</span>&#160;<span class="comment">//</span></div>
<div class="line"><a name="l00145"></a><span class="lineno">  145</span>&#160;<span class="comment">//    STB_TEXTEDIT_K_SHIFT       a power of two that is or&#39;d in to a keyboard input to represent the shift key</span></div>
<div class="line"><a name="l00146"></a><span class="lineno">  146</span>&#160;<span class="comment">//</span></div>
<div class="line"><a name="l00147"></a><span class="lineno">  147</span>&#160;<span class="comment">//    STB_TEXTEDIT_K_LEFT        keyboard input to move cursor left</span></div>
<div class="line"><a name="l00148"></a><span class="lineno">  148</span>&#160;<span class="comment">//    STB_TEXTEDIT_K_RIGHT       keyboard input to move cursor right</span></div>
<div class="line"><a name="l00149"></a><span class="lineno">  149</span>&#160;<span class="comment">//    STB_TEXTEDIT_K_UP          keyboard input to move cursor up</span></div>
<div class="line"><a name="l00150"></a><span class="lineno">  150</span>&#160;<span class="comment">//    STB_TEXTEDIT_K_DOWN        keyboard input to move cursor down</span></div>
<div class="line"><a name="l00151"></a><span class="lineno">  151</span>&#160;<span class="comment">//    STB_TEXTEDIT_K_LINESTART   keyboard input to move cursor to start of line  // e.g. HOME</span></div>
<div class="line"><a name="l00152"></a><span class="lineno">  152</span>&#160;<span class="comment">//    STB_TEXTEDIT_K_LINEEND     keyboard input to move cursor to end of line    // e.g. END</span></div>
<div class="line"><a name="l00153"></a><span class="lineno">  153</span>&#160;<span class="comment">//    STB_TEXTEDIT_K_TEXTSTART   keyboard input to move cursor to start of text  // e.g. ctrl-HOME</span></div>
<div class="line"><a name="l00154"></a><span class="lineno">  154</span>&#160;<span class="comment">//    STB_TEXTEDIT_K_TEXTEND     keyboard input to move cursor to end of text    // e.g. ctrl-END</span></div>
<div class="line"><a name="l00155"></a><span class="lineno">  155</span>&#160;<span class="comment">//    STB_TEXTEDIT_K_DELETE      keyboard input to delete selection or character under cursor</span></div>
<div class="line"><a name="l00156"></a><span class="lineno">  156</span>&#160;<span class="comment">//    STB_TEXTEDIT_K_BACKSPACE   keyboard input to delete selection or character left of cursor</span></div>
<div class="line"><a name="l00157"></a><span class="lineno">  157</span>&#160;<span class="comment">//    STB_TEXTEDIT_K_UNDO        keyboard input to perform undo</span></div>
<div class="line"><a name="l00158"></a><span class="lineno">  158</span>&#160;<span class="comment">//    STB_TEXTEDIT_K_REDO        keyboard input to perform redo</span></div>
<div class="line"><a name="l00159"></a><span class="lineno">  159</span>&#160;<span class="comment">//</span></div>
<div class="line"><a name="l00160"></a><span class="lineno">  160</span>&#160;<span class="comment">// Optional:</span></div>
<div class="line"><a name="l00161"></a><span class="lineno">  161</span>&#160;<span class="comment">//    STB_TEXTEDIT_K_INSERT              keyboard input to toggle insert mode</span></div>
<div class="line"><a name="l00162"></a><span class="lineno">  162</span>&#160;<span class="comment">//    STB_TEXTEDIT_IS_SPACE(ch)          true if character is whitespace (e.g. &#39;isspace&#39;),</span></div>
<div class="line"><a name="l00163"></a><span class="lineno">  163</span>&#160;<span class="comment">//                                          required for default WORDLEFT/WORDRIGHT handlers</span></div>
<div class="line"><a name="l00164"></a><span class="lineno">  164</span>&#160;<span class="comment">//    STB_TEXTEDIT_MOVEWORDLEFT(obj,i)   custom handler for WORDLEFT, returns index to move cursor to</span></div>

<div class="line"><a name="l00166"></a><span class="lineno">  166</span>&#160;<span class="comment">//    STB_TEXTEDIT_K_WORDLEFT            keyboard input to move cursor left one word // e.g. ctrl-LEFT</span></div>
<div class="line"><a name="l00167"></a><span class="lineno">  167</span>&#160;<span class="comment">//    STB_TEXTEDIT_K_WORDRIGHT           keyboard input to move cursor right one word // e.g. ctrl-RIGHT</span></div>

<div class="line"><a name="l00172"></a><span class="lineno">  172</span>&#160;<span class="comment">//</span></div>
<div class="line"><a name="l00173"></a><span class="lineno">  173</span>&#160;<span class="comment">// Todo:</span></div>
<div class="line"><a name="l00174"></a><span class="lineno">  174</span>&#160;<span class="comment">//    STB_TEXTEDIT_K_PGUP        keyboard input to move cursor up a page</span></div>
<div class="line"><a name="l00175"></a><span class="lineno">  175</span>&#160;<span class="comment">//    STB_TEXTEDIT_K_PGDOWN      keyboard input to move cursor down a page</span></div>
<div class="line"><a name="l00176"></a><span class="lineno">  176</span>&#160;<span class="comment">//</span></div>
<div class="line"><a name="l00177"></a><span class="lineno">  177</span>&#160;<span class="comment">// Keyboard input must be encoded as a single integer value; e.g. a character code</span></div>
<div class="line"><a name="l00178"></a><span class="lineno">  178</span>&#160;<span class="comment">// and some bitflags that represent shift states. to simplify the interface, SHIFT must</span></div>
<div class="line"><a name="l00179"></a><span class="lineno">  179</span>&#160;<span class="comment">// be a bitflag, so we can test the shifted state of cursor movements to allow selection,</span></div>
<div class="line"><a name="l00180"></a><span class="lineno">  180</span>&#160;<span class="comment">// i.e. (STB_TEXTED_K_RIGHT|STB_TEXTEDIT_K_SHIFT) should be shifted right-arrow.</span></div>
<div class="line"><a name="l00181"></a><span class="lineno">  181</span>&#160;<span class="comment">//</span></div>
<div class="line"><a name="l00182"></a><span class="lineno">  182</span>&#160;<span class="comment">// You can encode other things, such as CONTROL or ALT, in additional bits, and</span></div>
<div class="line"><a name="l00183"></a><span class="lineno">  183</span>&#160;<span class="comment">// then test for their presence in e.g. STB_TEXTEDIT_K_WORDLEFT. For example,</span></div>
<div class="line"><a name="l00184"></a><span class="lineno">  184</span>&#160;<span class="comment">// my Windows implementations add an additional CONTROL bit, and an additional KEYDOWN</span></div>
<div class="line"><a name="l00185"></a><span class="lineno">  185</span>&#160;<span class="comment">// bit. Then all of the STB_TEXTEDIT_K_ values bitwise-or in the KEYDOWN bit,</span></div>
<div class="line"><a name="l00186"></a><span class="lineno">  186</span>&#160;<span class="comment">// and I pass both WM_KEYDOWN and WM_CHAR events to the &quot;key&quot; function in the</span></div>
<div class="line"><a name="l00187"></a><span class="lineno">  187</span>&#160;<span class="comment">// API below. The control keys will only match WM_KEYDOWN events because of the</span></div>
<div class="line"><a name="l00188"></a><span class="lineno">  188</span>&#160;<span class="comment">// keydown bit I add, and STB_TEXTEDIT_KEYTOTEXT only tests for the KEYDOWN</span></div>
<div class="line"><a name="l00189"></a><span class="lineno">  189</span>&#160;<span class="comment">// bit so it only decodes WM_CHAR events.</span></div>
<div class="line"><a name="l00190"></a><span class="lineno">  190</span>&#160;<span class="comment">//</span></div>
<div class="line"><a name="l00191"></a><span class="lineno">  191</span>&#160;<span class="comment">// STB_TEXTEDIT_LAYOUTROW returns information about the shape of one displayed</span></div>
<div class="line"><a name="l00192"></a><span class="lineno">  192</span>&#160;<span class="comment">// row of characters assuming they start on the i&#39;th character--the width and</span></div>
<div class="line"><a name="l00193"></a><span class="lineno">  193</span>&#160;<span class="comment">// the height and the number of characters consumed. This allows this library</span></div>
<div class="line"><a name="l00194"></a><span class="lineno">  194</span>&#160;<span class="comment">// to traverse the entire layout incrementally. You need to compute word-wrapping</span></div>
<div class="line"><a name="l00195"></a><span class="lineno">  195</span>&#160;<span class="comment">// here.</span></div>
<div class="line"><a name="l00196"></a><span class="lineno">  196</span>&#160;<span class="comment">//</span></div>
<div class="line"><a name="l00197"></a><span class="lineno">  197</span>&#160;<span class="comment">// Each textfield keeps its own insert mode state, which is not how normal</span></div>
<div class="line"><a name="l00198"></a><span class="lineno">  198</span>&#160;<span class="comment">// applications work. To keep an app-wide insert mode, update/copy the</span></div>
<div class="line"><a name="l00199"></a><span class="lineno">  199</span>&#160;<span class="comment">// &quot;insert_mode&quot; field of STB_TexteditState before/after calling API functions.</span></div>
<div class="line"><a name="l00200"></a><span class="lineno">  200</span>&#160;<span class="comment">//</span></div>
<div class="line"><a name="l00201"></a><span class="lineno">  201</span>&#160;<span class="comment">// API</span></div>

<div class="line"><a name="l00203"></a><span class="lineno">  203</span>&#160;<span class="comment">//    void stb_textedit_initialize_state(STB_TexteditState *state, int is_single_line)</span></div>
<div class="line"><a name="l00204"></a><span class="lineno">  204</span>&#160;<span class="comment">//</span></div>
<div class="line"><a name="l00205"></a><span class="lineno">  205</span>&#160;<span class="comment">//    void stb_textedit_click(STB_TEXTEDIT_STRING *str, STB_TexteditState *state, float x, float y)</span></div>

<div class="line"><a name="l00245"></a><span class="lineno">  245</span>&#160;<span class="comment">//</span></div>

<div class="line"><a name="l00256"></a><span class="lineno">  256</span>&#160;<span class="comment">// layout incrementally--we try to make sure we make as few passes through</span></div>

<div class="line"><a name="l00263"></a><span class="lineno">  263</span>&#160;<span class="comment">//</span></div>
<div class="line"><a name="l00264"></a><span class="lineno">  264</span>&#160;<span class="comment">// If it&#39;s run in a widget that *has* cached the layout, then this is less</span></div>

<div class="line"><a name="l00409"></a><span class="lineno">  409</span>&#160;      STB_TEXTEDIT_LAYOUTROW(&amp;r, str, i);</div>
<div class="line"><a name="l00410"></a><span class="lineno">  410</span>&#160;      <span class="keywordflow">if</span> (r.num_chars &lt;= 0)</div>
<div class="line"><a name="l00411"></a><span class="lineno">  411</span>&#160;         <span class="keywordflow">return</span> n;</div>

<div class="line"><a name="l00428"></a><span class="lineno">  428</span>&#160;   <span class="keywordflow">if</span> (x &lt; r.x0)</div>
